questions.stem: Which law states that the potential difference across a conductor is directly proportional to the current through it, provided the temperature remains constant?
questions.solution: Ohm’s law states that the potential difference across a conductor is directly proportional to the current through it, provided the temperature remains constant. Kirchhoff’s law deals with the conservation of charge and energy in circuits, Faraday’s law relates to electromagnetic induction, and Newton’s law is related to motion and force in physics.

questions.stem: What happens to the current in a circuit when a thicker wire is used instead of a thinner one, assuming all other factors are the same?
questions.solution: The current increases because a thicker wire has a larger cross-sectional area, which reduces resistance and allows more current to flow. A pupil who thinks resistance increases with thickness might choose 'It decreases'. A pupil who misunderstands the relationship between resistance and current might choose 'It remains the same'. A pupil who thinks current stops entirely might choose 'It becomes zero'.

questions.stem: What does the term 'electric current' refer to?
choices: The flow of electrons in a conductor
The potential difference between two points
The flow of positive charges in a conductor
The flow of protons in a conductor
questions.solution: Electric current refers to the flow of electric charges, usually electrons, through a conductor. Potential difference is the work done to move a charge, resistance is the opposition to current flow, and energy consumed by a bulb is a result of current and voltage.

questions.stem: What is the SI unit of electric resistance?
questions.solution: The SI unit of electric resistance is Ohm. Volt is the unit of potential difference, Ampere is the unit of electric current, and Watt is the unit of power. A pupil might confuse these units if they do not remember the definitions clearly.

questions.stem: If a nichrome wire is replaced by a copper wire of the same dimensions in a circuit, what will happen to the current?
questions.solution: Copper has a lower resistivity compared to nichrome. Since resistance is directly proportional to resistivity, replacing a nichrome wire with a copper wire of the same dimensions will reduce the resistance in the circuit. A lower resistance allows more current to flow, so the current will increase. The option 'It will increase' is correct. The other options suggest no change or a decrease, which contradicts the fact that copper is a better conductor than nichrome.

hi.stem: यदि एक निक्रोम के तार को एक तांबे के तार से बदल दिया जाए जिसके आयाम समान हों, तो परिपथ में धारा क्या होगी?
hi.solution: तांबा निक्रोम की तुलना में कम प्रतिरोधकता रखता है। प्रतिरोध प्रतिरोधकता के सीधे आनुपातिक होता है, अतः निक्रोम के तार के स्थान पर आयाम समान तांबे के तार के उपयोग से परिपथ में प्रतिरोध कम हो जाएगा। कम प्रतिरोध अधिक धारा प्रवाहित होने की अनुमति देता है, अतः धारा बढ़ जाएगी। विकल्प 'यह बढ़ जाएगी' सही है। अन्य विकल्प बिना किसी बदलाव या कमी का संकेत देते हैं, जो तांबे के निक्रोम की तुलना में अच्छा चालक होने के तथ्य के विरोधी हैं।

mr.stem: जर निक्रोमच्या तारेच्या बदल्यात एका तारेच्या त्याच आकाराच्या तारेचा वापर केला जाईल, तर परिपथातील विद्युतप्रवाह काय होईल?

questions.stem: In a circuit, a resistor has a current of 5 A and a resistance of 4 Ω. What is the potential difference across the resistor?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 20 V. Using Ohm's law, V = I × R = 5 A × 4 Ω = 20 V. The other options result from incorrect multiplication or addition of the values.

hi.stem: एक परिपथ में, एक प्रतिरोधक में 5 एम्पियर की धारा तथा 4 ओम का प्रतिरोध है। प्रतिरोधक के आर-पार विभवांतर क्या है?
hi.solution: सही उत्तर 20 वोल्ट है। ओम के नियम के अनुसार, V = I × R = 5 एम्पियर × 4 ओम = 20 वोल्ट। अन्य विकल्प दिए गए मानों के गलत गुणा या जोड़ के कारण प्राप्त होते हैं।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation is accurate, maintains the same meaning, and uses standard technical terms as found in Hindi-medium textbooks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the resistivity of a material?
choices: It depends on the length of the conductor
It depends on the cross-sectional area of the conductor
It is a property of the material itself
It changes with the temperature of the conductor
questions.solution: Resistivity is an intrinsic property of a material and does not depend on the dimensions of the conductor. The length and cross-sectional area of a conductor affect resistance, not resistivity. Temperature can influence resistivity, but the statement that it is a property of the material itself is correct because it remains constant for a given material under consistent conditions.

questions.stem: A resistor of 4 Ω is replaced with a wire of half the length and double the cross-sectional area. What is the new resistance?
questions.solution: Resistance R is proportional to length and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area. Halving the length halves the resistance, and doubling the cross-sectional area halves it again. So the new resistance is 4 Ω / 4 = 1 Ω. The other options are incorrect as they do not account for both changes in length and area.

hi.stem: 4 ओम के एक प्रतिरोधक को आधी लंबाई और दोगुने अनुप्रस्थ काट के तार से बदल दिया जाता है। नया प्रतिरोध क्या है?
hi.solution: प्रतिरोध R लंबाई के समानुपाती और अनुप्रस्थ काट के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है। लंबाई के आधा होने से प्रतिरोध आधा हो जाता है और अनुप्रस्थ काट के दोगुना होने से प्रतिरोध फिर से आधा हो जाता है। अतः नया प्रतिरोध 4 ओम / 4 = 1 ओम है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि वे लंबाई और क्षेत्रफल में दोनों परिवर्तनों को ध्यान में नहीं रखते।

mr.stem: 4 Ω चा प्रतिरोधक अर्धा लांबी आणि दुप्पट अनुलंब क्षेत्रफळ असलेल्या तारेने बदलला जातो. नवीन प्रतिरोध किती असेल?
mr.solution: प्रतिरोध R लांबीच्या आणि अनुलंब क्षेत्रफळाच्या व्यस्त प्रमाणात असतो. लांबीचा अर्धा केल्यामुळे प्रतिरोध अर्धा होतो आणि अनुलंब क्षेत्रफळ दुप्पट केल्यामुळे पुन्हा अर्धा होतो. म्हणून नवीन प्रतिरोध 4 Ω / 4 = 1 Ω असेल. इतर विकल्प चुकीचे असतील कारण ते लांबी आणि क्षेत्रफळाच्या दोन्ही बदलांचा विचार करत नाहीत.
